title: Factoring a finitely presented algebra through B/J, B smooth, J in IB (square-zero base)
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\Lambda$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $I\subset R$ an ideal. Assume (1) $I^2=0$ and (2) $\Lambda/I\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R/I$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. Let $A$ be a finitely presented $R$-algebra ($A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ as $R$-algebras) and $\varphi:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras. Then there are a smooth $R$-algebra $B$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], a finitely generated ideal $J\subset B$ with $J\subset IB$ ($IB$ the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $I$), and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\psi:A\to B/J$ and $\chi:B/J\to\Lambda$ with $\chi\circ\psi=\varphi$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, line 1238) and its proof (lines 1255-1303: Lemma Tag 07CI lemma-colimit-standard-smooth, Algebra Proposition 00TN, Algebra Lemma 00DV NAK, Algebra Lemma 00R2 finite-presentation-independent)

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-once-core to obtain the finitely presented intermediary A' and a smooth B with an R-algebra isomorphism e : B/IB ≅ A'/IA'. This is only the presentation part (old steps 1--8).

Since I²=0, Ideal.map_pow gives (IA')²=0. Compose e with the quotient map B → B/IB and use Algebra.FormallySmooth.comp_surjective to obtain θ : B → A' lifting this composite. Smoothness supplies formal smoothness.

Transport module quotients by I • top to the ideal quotients using Ideal.smul_top_eq_map and Submodule.quotEquivOfEq. The reduction of θ is e, hence surjective. Apply RingTheory.surjective_of_surjective_mod_nilpotent with exponent 2 to obtain surjectivity of θ.

Set J = ker θ. Both B (by smoothness) and A' are finitely presented, so Mathlib Algebra.FinitePresentation.ker_fG_of_surjective gives J.FG directly. This is the general surjection version of the polynomial-presentation kernel argument (old step 11).
For b ∈ J, reduction of θ(b)=0 says e(b mod IB)=0. Injectivity of e gives b ∈ IB, so J ≤ IB.

Use Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective to identify B/J with A'. Compose its inverse with ι and compose it with φ'. An AlgHom.ext calculation using q(q⁻¹(ι(x)))=ι(x) and φ'∘ι=φ verifies the factorization.
